response.markdown_report:
The best first direction is a **gated mixture of SASRec and recency-weighted history pooling**, evaluated through controlled history perturbations. At 0% research progress, this offers a small, testable change before attempting semantic compatibility reasoning.

**Insights from the starting point.**

1. Qualitative feedback favors recent, repeated, specific interests. This motivates testing history aggregation, but does not establish that stronger recency weighting improves HR@10.
2. Existing margins measure separation against sampled training negatives. They cannot establish generalization or explain full-catalog recommendation quality.
3. Compatibility and satisfied needs are plausible concerns. Available histories and descriptions cannot establish ownership, prerequisites, or current intent, so unknown evidence must remain unknown.

**Insights from related work.**

1. [Does It Look Sequential?](https://doi.org/10.1145/3640457.3688195) motivates testing whether ordering contributes beyond history membership. Earlier-item shuffling with the last item fixed can probe this distinction.
2. [Measuring Recency Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) cautions against assuming recent items deserve greater weight. Any recency mechanism therefore needs comparison with uniform pooling.
3. [Sampling reliability research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) shows evaluation sampling can affect conclusions. The pinned macro validation HR@10 must remain the selection objective; diagnostic rankings are supplementary.

These insights organize three directions: measure order dependence, improve aggregation, and calibrate evidence limits.

| Direction | Existing component | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Order | SASRec sequence features | Last-item-fixed shuffle probe | Sensitivity does not establish intent |
| Aggregation | Final sequence representation | Gated recency pooling | Excessive recency can hurt |
| Calibration | Training-negative margins | Paired validation hit differences | Adaptive selection uncertainty remains |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled shuffle audit: 3/7/2.** Positive: cheap, interpretable comparison grounded in sequence-shuffling research. Negative: diagnostic only; no direct ranking improvement.
- **Gated recency pooling: 4/8/4.** Positive: combines order-sensitive and aggregated history evidence with a small architectural change. Negative: familiar components and possible redundancy with SASRec.
- **Evidence-backed compatibility adjustment: 6/6/8.** Positive: addresses functional fit, motivated by [ECCR](https://www.amazon.science/publications/eccr-explainable-and-coherent-complement-recommendation-based-on-large-language-models). Negative: sparse descriptions and uncertain compatibility make reliable scoring expensive.

Select gated pooling. For each prefix, combine its SASRec state with a normalized recency-weighted mean of item embeddings using one learned scalar gate per dataset. Initialize the mixture near SASRec; retain the baseline loss initially to isolate architectural effects.

```text
h = SASRec(prefix)
p = recency_pool(item_embeddings(prefix), padding_mask)
z = (1 - sigmoid(g)) * h + sigmoid(g) * normalize(p)
score(candidate) = dot(z, item_embedding(candidate))
```

Compare baseline, uniform pooling, and recency pooling within the shared budget. Select using equally weighted validation HR@10 across all four datasets. Report paired user-bootstrap differences as conditional uncertainty, without claiming training-seed robustness. Preserve diagnostic interfaces, restore model mode after probes, and update the predictor writer to reproduce the mixture exactly.

idea.description: Add a learned scalar gate per dataset that mixes SASRec sequence states with a normalized recency-weighted mean of observed item embeddings.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests that recent and repeated interests may be underused. A minimal aggregation branch tests this hypothesis without inferring unavailable traits, ownership, or compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl and their routing. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and train on one GPU. Use only training prefixes for pooling; mask padding and future positions during per-position training. Normalize pooled vectors with LayerNorm and initialize sigmoid(g) near 0.05. Compare uniform weighting with one fixed modest recency decay before expanding the search. Save gate, normalization, decay, and architecture configuration; update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs identical scoring. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Expose the actual model through view.model and mixed features through log2feats; retain item_emb and predict_score compatibility. Define every reported metric, restore the prior train/eval mode, and omit unavailable metadata-based probes. Select solely by the pinned macro validation HR@10. Full-catalog recommendations for the twenty training users are exposure audits, not accuracy estimates. No experiments or measured improvements are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset:
  construct baseline SASRec and a learned scalar gate g
  for each training batch:
    h = SASRec(sequence)
    p = causal_weighted_prefix_mean(item_emb(sequence), padding_mask, decay)
    z = (1 - sigmoid(g)) * h + sigmoid(g) * LayerNorm(p)
    compute baseline loss from positive/negative dot-product scores at valid positions
    update model and gate
  evaluate through the pinned validation protocol
  save model weights and complete predictor configuration
Compare against baseline and uniform-pooling variants; select by four-category macro HR@10.

originality.positive: The diagnostic-to-aggregation connection gives a concrete, falsifiable response to the supplied feedback.
originality.negative: Mixing sequential representations with pooled histories uses established architectural components.

future_potential.positive: A successful minimal branch could motivate better history aggregation and controlled studies of recency versus order.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may depend on dataset sparsity and candidate sampling, limiting generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires one pooling branch, a scalar gate, and a small inference update.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal prefix pooling, padding handling, feature scaling, and predictor parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Uses sequence shuffling to investigate the importance of sequential structure across recommendation datasets.
Motivates order-sensitivity controls alongside aggregation baselines.
limitations: Its reported findings do not establish the behavior of the four matched Amazon datasets.
Shuffle sensitivity alone does not identify user intent or explain recommendation correctness.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Introduces a dedicated recency metric and investigates excessive emphasis on recent interactions.
Motivates testing recency weighting against uniform history aggregation.
limitations: Does not justify universally increasing recency weights.
Does not establish an optimal decay for this benchmark.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: Studies sampling reliability through agreement with full ranking, discrimination, robustness, and recovery of model rankings.
Supports treating sampled diagnostic rankings as conditional evidence.
limitations: Does not validate the supplied training-margin diagnostics as predictors of validation misses.
Does not authorize modifying the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: ECCR: Explainable and Coherent Complement Recommendation Based on Large Language Models
contributions: Distinguishes coherent complementarity from co-purchase frequency.
Motivates checking functional relationships when sufficient item evidence exists.
limitations: Functional complementarity does not establish specific interface compatibility.
The supplied task lacks sufficient evidence to infer ownership or unmet needs reliably.
